item.content:encoded:
I like the concept of this overall, and I think it's just good enough to get an up-vote from me.

But I will agree on this being able to be improved a bit. I think a few more tests to discern the extent of the creatures strength (cut-resistant armour, for example) and perhaps a conclusion to the proposed final test. If I was going to suggest anything in particular, perhaps adjust the tone of the research staff in the logs too? They don't seem clinical/professional enough IMO.

My interpretation of the entities was that they are almost a meta representation of the readers of the SCP world, moving about unseen, observing their world, reading their files. I think that's why this managed to hook me as a concept.

It also made me think of the SCP that is triggered into attacking when information about it is recorded. Since they only seem hostile to people who have been directly made aware of their existence. But I like being able to build parallels between SCPs, others might not.

item.content:encoded:
Sorry, bit late to reply but:

I think you've missed the point of this article.

The idea is that the entities ARE everywhere and our actions seem to naturally flow around the creatures. In other words, I could run about this room, flailing my arms but by way of an unknown phenomena, they would be out of reach at all times.

This changes when a person is made AWARE of an entity's presence. By knowing it is there, you have broken the natural state of things. You can now interact with them because you know where they are and how to avoid the natural avoidance.

I guess it's similar to Superposition, in that, the creature can be considered both there and not there at the same time. It's not until they're observed that it can be confirmed where they are and therefore interacted with.

I think it could also partly be considered a 'memetic hazard', in that the knowledge of their placement is what puts you in danger. If I put on the glasses and say 'there's one right behind you', you'll now know it's there and therefore be in danger of interacting with it. Had you have not know, you'd have naturally avoided it. Now you know, your actions will be altered to avoid it and may inadvertently lead to you touching it (which is why it's a very scary concept).

Point is: It heavily implies we, as a part of our defined existence, avoid these creatures. By being made aware, we break that state and put ourselves in danger.

Any attempt by the wearer or any other personnel (see Incident Report #178-14-Alpha) to directly interact with the entities results in severe lacerations suddenly appearing on persons involved

If these things attack if they're touched by people who aren't wearing the SCP, then… why aren't people dying all over the world from random lacerations? It seems utterly impossible that the entities are apparently everywhere (since people wearing the SCP always view them) yet only when wearing the glasses and interacting do they retaliate. None of this makes any sense; if people who aren't wearing the SCP can interact and be killed by these things, wouldn't this cause millions of deaths every day all around the world from accidental bumping or people talking to themselves? Seems pointlessly cruel and just needlessly gorey for them to just start killing the shit out of everything that mildly touches them, regardless of whether they have the SCP on or not.

Unless there's only two of them and they only ever follow the SCP. Except that's not even hinted at anywhere in the article.

Makes it even worse that the document that is ABSOLUTELY REQUIRED READING OR ELSE FACE DISCIPLINARY ACTION apparently doesn't exist.

I really like the concept, but it just seems to me that all this thing offers is lots of pointless gore, evidenced by the experiment log.

item.content:encoded:
I think Wartheim's argument is that it's Euclid because we don't understand how the glasses interact with the entities. I disagree, because the one thing we do understand is that the glasses only (seem to) become dangerous when they're actively worn by a human (so far). In general, they pass the "lock them in a room" test for 'safe'.

As for the argument that this is like SCP-750 - I'll admit the conceptual similarity, but a) I think the similarity is vague enough that these are effectively separate notions, and b) this one is better. 750 just makes you see (and otherwise sense) shit that ain't there. That's quite definite. They're just schizophrenia-inducing.

The shit that this makes you see… most definitely is there. The thematic connection with SCP-362 is stronger (so much so that part of my brain is saying CROSS-TEST THEM!), but I still feel that these are distinct enough.

You know what might be interesting? If these had a "THE FACTORY" logo on them. Imagine how many other people there are who have a pair of these glasses…
